findings: No hook payload carries the selected output style, and none carries `model` (SessionStart keys: cwd, hook_event_name, session_id, source, transcript_path). A hook cannot establish main-thread policy_on or profile from its input.
Every event carries `prompt_id`; tool events carry `tool_use_id`. SubagentStart exists and carries agent_id and agent_type.

Tool events fired INSIDE a subagent carry agent_id and agent_type and share the parent's session_id — same as Codex (era 99 A2). Per-session tool accumulation mixes subagent tools into the main thread unless split by agent_id.

SubagentStop.last_assistant_message was a stub ('I sent my report to the agent that started me.'). The subagent's report travelled through a `SubagentHandback` tool call: its PostToolUse tool_input.message holds the report, with agent_id.
The report then reached the orchestrator as a second UserPromptSubmit whose prompt begins '<agent-message from=…>'. The current logger would overwrite `task` with it.
The Agent tool's PostToolUse tool_input.prompt is the delegation prompt (coding.19's subject); tool_response also echoes it with agentId and agentType.
Whether the handback route is always taken, or depends on this build or account configuration, was not established. Era 01 (2.1.270) recorded real subagent text in SubagentStop.
